hook: People adoption vs. controlled project change
leftMeaning: Helps people understand, adopt, and sustain a new way of working. Think resistance, communication, training, engagement, readiness, and reinforcement.
rightMeaning: Evaluates and governs proposed changes to controlled project elements such as baselines, scope, schedule, or cost. Think impact analysis, change request, approval authority, updates, and implementation.
trap: Do not use formal change control as the answer to a people-resistance problem. Do not treat organizational adoption as permission to alter a project baseline.
memory: CHANGE MANAGEMENT = people adopt. CHANGE CONTROL = project changes are governed.

leftMeaning: Focuses on how people adopt a new capability, process, system, or behavior.
rightMeaning: Focuses on changes to the project or product and the impact on plans, requirements, baselines, cost, schedule, risk, or governance.
trap: A system rollout facing employee resistance is not automatically a baseline-change problem.
memory: People resist → organizational change. Baseline affected → project change/control.

leftMeaning: An uncertain future event or condition that may affect objectives.
rightMeaning: A current problem or event that has already occurred and requires action.
trap: Once the event has happened, continuing to treat it only as a future risk delays action.
memory: MAY HAPPEN = Risk Register. HAPPENED = Issue Log.

leftMeaning: Describes HOW an area of the project will be planned, managed, monitored, or controlled.
rightMeaning: The approved reference point used to compare actual performance for controlled scope, schedule, or cost.
trap: A plan and a baseline are not interchangeable. Updating a management approach is different from changing an approved performance target.
memory: PLAN = HOW. BASELINE = APPROVED.

leftMeaning: A formal proposal to modify a document, deliverable, baseline, process, or other controlled element.
rightMeaning: Tracks the status and disposition of change requests over time.
trap: Logging a change request does not mean it has been approved.
memory: REQUEST asks for change. LOG tracks what happened to the request.

hook: Internally correct vs. customer formally accepted
leftMeaning: Has been checked for correctness and conformance to requirements through quality control.
rightMeaning: Has received formal acceptance from the customer, sponsor, or authorized stakeholder.
trap: Passing internal quality checks does not equal formal customer acceptance.
memory: VERIFY = we checked it. ACCEPT = they approved it.

leftMeaning: Checks deliverables for correctness, completeness, and conformance to quality requirements.
rightMeaning: Obtains formal acceptance of completed deliverables from the appropriate stakeholder.
trap: Do not ask the customer to formally accept a deliverable before it has been appropriately checked.
memory: QUALITY checks it. SCOPE accepts it.

hook: Why invest vs. how value will be realized
leftMeaning: Explains why the initiative is worth doing and supports the investment decision.
rightMeaning: Defines expected benefits, how and when they will be measured, and who owns realization.
trap: Finishing the deliverable does not prove the business benefits were achieved.
memory: BUSINESS CASE = WHY. BENEFITS = WHAT VALUE, WHEN, HOW MEASURED, WHO OWNS IT.

hook: Who may decide vs. what must be followed
leftMeaning: Defines decision rights, authority, oversight, escalation paths, and who can approve what.
rightMeaning: Deals with mandatory laws, regulations, standards, policies, safety, audit, or other obligations.
trap: Governance tells you who decides. Compliance tells you what cannot simply be ignored or traded away.
memory: GOVERNANCE = WHO DECIDES. COMPLIANCE = WHAT MUST BE FOLLOWED.

hook: Improve it vs. add to it
leftMeaning: Refines the same solution through repeated versions or cycles.
rightMeaning: Adds usable pieces of the solution over time.
trap: Repeated prototypes that get better are iterative; delivering additional usable features in pieces is incremental.
memory: ITERATIVE improves. INCREMENTAL adds.

leftMeaning: Uses frequent feedback, adaptation, small increments, collaboration, and evolving requirements.
rightMeaning: Deliberately combines predictive and adaptive techniques because different parts of the work need different controls.
trap: Hybrid is not random mixing and Agile is not the absence of planning or control.
memory: AGILE = learn and adapt. HYBRID = blend what fits.

leftMeaning: Inspects the product/increment and discusses progress and next product directions with stakeholders.
rightMeaning: Inspects how the team worked and identifies improvements to teamwork and process.
trap: Stakeholder product feedback belongs in the Review; team process improvement belongs in the Retrospective.
memory: REVIEW = product. RETRO = process.

hook: Product priorities vs. current Sprint plan
leftMeaning: Ordered, evolving list of product work and needs.
rightMeaning: The Developers' plan for the Sprint: Sprint Goal, selected work, and the plan for delivering it.
trap: Do not treat the Sprint Backlog as a permanently frozen contract; it can evolve as more is learned while protecting the Sprint Goal.
memory: PRODUCT BACKLOG = what may come. SPRINT BACKLOG = what the team is working through now.

hook: Who they are vs. how to engage them
leftMeaning: Identifies stakeholders and records relevant characteristics such as interest, influence, or impact.
rightMeaning: Defines strategies and actions for engaging stakeholders effectively.
trap: Identifying a stakeholder is not the same as planning how to influence or involve them.
memory: REGISTER = WHO. ENGAGEMENT PLAN = HOW.

leftMeaning: Requirements Traceability Matrix links requirements from origin through delivery, verification, and acceptance.
rightMeaning: Work Breakdown Structure decomposes the total project scope into manageable components/work packages.
trap: RTM is not a task tracker and WBS is not a requirements traceability tool.
memory: RTM = TRACE requirements. WBS = BREAK DOWN scope.

leftMeaning: Hierarchical decomposition of project scope.
rightMeaning: Provides detailed information about WBS components/work packages.
trap: Do not expect the WBS graphic alone to carry all descriptive detail.
memory: WBS = structure. WBS DICTIONARY = detail.

leftMeaning: Request for Information: used to learn about supplier capabilities, offerings, or the market before defining a procurement approach.
rightMeaning: Request for Proposal: asks sellers to propose how they would solve or deliver against stated needs, often when solution approach matters.
trap: Do not use an RFP merely to gather basic market information.
memory: RFI = tell me what is possible. RFP = propose how you would solve it.

leftMeaning: Used when the buyer needs sellers to propose an approach or solution.
rightMeaning: Request for Quotation: used when specifications are clear and price is a primary comparison factor.
trap: Clear standard specifications plus price emphasis point toward an RFQ, not a broad proposal.
memory: RFP = propose. RFQ = quote.

hook: What was delivered vs. what changed
leftMeaning: The product, service, result, or deliverable produced.
rightMeaning: The effect created when users or the organization actually use the output.
trap: A delivered system can exist without producing the intended business outcome.
memory: OUTPUT = we delivered it. OUTCOME = something changed because it was used.

leftMeaning: The result of using the deliverable, such as customers shifting to self-service.
rightMeaning: The measurable improvement created by the outcome, such as lower support cost or faster service.
trap: Do not call the deliverable itself the benefit.
memory: OUTPUT → OUTCOME → BENEFIT → VALUE.

leftMeaning: Budget held for identified risks and known-unknowns that have been analyzed and planned for.
rightMeaning: Budget held outside the cost baseline for unforeseen work or unknown-unknown uncertainty.
trap: Do not treat management reserve as the default funding source for an identified risk response.
memory: CONTINGENCY = identified risk. MANAGEMENT RESERVE = unforeseen uncertainty.

leftMeaning: Ranks or prioritizes individual risks using relative assessments such as probability, impact, urgency, or other characteristics.
rightMeaning: Uses numerical techniques to evaluate uncertainty and its aggregate effect on objectives, such as simulations, decision trees, or EMV.
trap: A probability-impact matrix is qualitative; numerical monetary/schedule modeling is quantitative.
memory: QUALITATIVE = prioritize. QUANTITATIVE = calculate/model.

leftMeaning: A risk that could negatively affect objectives.
rightMeaning: A risk that could positively affect objectives.
trap: Do not assume every risk should be avoided; positive risks may be exploited, enhanced, or shared.
memory: THREAT hurts. OPPORTUNITY helps.

hook: Win-win vs. each side gives something up
leftMeaning: Works toward a solution that addresses the underlying concerns of all parties and seeks a durable win-win outcome.
rightMeaning: Finds a middle ground where each party gives up something to reach an acceptable solution.
trap: Compromise is not the same as collaboration; it usually leaves some needs partially unmet.
memory: COLLABORATE = solve fully. COMPROMISE = split the difference.

leftMeaning: Influence earned because others trust a person's expertise, experience, or technical knowledge.
rightMeaning: Influence earned because others respect, admire, or identify with the person.
trap: Both are personal powers, but one comes from competence and the other from relationships/respect.
memory: EXPERT = what you know. REFERENT = how people regard you.

leftMeaning: Focuses on serving the team, removing impediments, coaching, facilitating, and enabling self-management.
rightMeaning: Provides explicit direction and close guidance, useful when urgency, safety, or low team maturity requires it.
trap: Do not default to command-and-control when the team can solve the problem collaboratively.
memory: SERVANT = enable. DIRECTIVE = tell.

leftMeaning: The buyer/project team creates solicitation and selection artifacts such as procurement SOW, source-selection criteria, RFI, RFQ, RFP, or IFB.
rightMeaning: The seller/vendor creates the corresponding information response, quotation, proposal, bid, invoices, and delivery/status material.
trap: Do not confuse an RFP with the proposal that a seller submits in response.
memory: BUYER asks. SELLER responds.

hook: Seller cost risk vs. buyer cost risk
leftMeaning: Price is largely fixed for defined work; cost overrun risk generally falls more heavily on the seller.
rightMeaning: Buyer reimburses allowable costs plus an agreed fee or incentive structure; cost risk generally falls more heavily on the buyer.
trap: Do not choose contract type by habit; match it to scope certainty and risk allocation.
memory: FIXED PRICE = seller bears more cost risk. COST REIMBURSABLE = buyer bears more.

hook: Should we outsource vs. which seller should we choose
leftMeaning: Evaluates whether work should be performed internally or procured externally.
rightMeaning: Evaluates qualified sellers against approved source-selection criteria after the procurement strategy is established.
trap: Do not start comparing vendors before deciding whether external procurement is the right approach.
memory: MAKE/BUY = internal or external? SOURCE SELECTION = which seller?

hook: Return percentage vs. value in today's money
leftMeaning: Measures return relative to cost, commonly expressed as a percentage.
rightMeaning: Measures present value of future cash flows after discounting and considering investment/costs.
trap: Higher ROI and higher NPV can both be attractive, but they answer different financial questions.
memory: ROI = return rate. NPV = value today.

hook: Value forgone vs. money already spent
leftMeaning: The value of the best alternative you give up when choosing another option.
rightMeaning: A past cost that has already been incurred and should not drive a forward-looking decision simply because it has been spent.
trap: Do not continue a weak project merely to justify money already spent.
memory: OPPORTUNITY COST = what you gave up. SUNK COST = already gone.

hook: Investment asset spend vs. ongoing operating spend
leftMeaning: Capital expenditure for acquiring, creating, or improving long-lived assets or capabilities.
rightMeaning: Operating expenditure for ongoing operations, maintenance, support, and day-to-day running costs.
trap: A low purchase price can still create high long-term OPEX and poor lifecycle value.
memory: CAPEX = acquire/build. OPEX = operate/run.

hook: Improve the process vs. inspect/measure results
leftMeaning: Focuses on translating the quality plan into executable quality activities and improving processes during execution.
rightMeaning: Measures, inspects, and verifies results to determine whether deliverables and outputs meet quality requirements.
trap: Do not use inspection of finished outputs as a substitute for building quality into the process.
memory: MANAGE QUALITY = improve how we work. CONTROL QUALITY = check what we produced.

leftMeaning: Designs work and processes so defects are less likely to occur in the first place.
rightMeaning: Examines outputs to detect defects after or while work is being produced.
trap: Quality thinking generally favors prevention over relying only on inspection.
memory: PREVENTION stops defects. INSPECTION finds defects.

leftMeaning: Degree to which requirements are fulfilled and the result is fit for its intended use.
rightMeaning: Category or level assigned to products/services with different technical characteristics or feature sets.
trap: Low grade can still be high quality if it meets its stated requirements; high grade can still be poor quality.
memory: QUALITY = meets requirements. GRADE = feature/class level.

hook: Planned work value vs. completed work value
leftMeaning: Planned Value: budgeted value of work that should have been completed by a point in time.
rightMeaning: Earned Value: budgeted value of work actually completed.
trap: PV is not actual spending and EV is not money paid.
memory: PV = what should be done. EV = what was actually completed, valued at budget.

leftMeaning: Earned Value represents the budgeted value of completed work.
rightMeaning: Actual Cost is what the project actually spent to perform the work.
trap: EV < AC means the project has spent more than the budgeted value of the work earned.
memory: EV = earned work value. AC = actual money spent.

leftMeaning: Cost Performance Index = EV ÷ AC. Below 1 indicates cost inefficiency/over budget relative to earned value.
rightMeaning: Schedule Performance Index = EV ÷ PV. Below 1 indicates less work accomplished than planned.
trap: CPI talks about cost; SPI talks about schedule progress.
memory: CPI = cost. SPI = schedule.

leftMeaning: Estimate at Completion forecasts total expected project cost when all work is finished.
rightMeaning: Estimate to Complete forecasts the additional cost needed from now until completion.
trap: Do not report the remaining cost (ETC) as if it were the total final forecast (EAC).
memory: EAC = all-in finish cost. ETC = what's left to spend.

leftMeaning: A temporary effort with a defined beginning/end that creates a unique product, service, result, or change.
rightMeaning: Ongoing, repetitive work that sustains the business or delivers routine services.
trap: Temporary does not mean short; a multi-year effort can still be a project if it has a defined end.
memory: PROJECT = change. OPERATIONS = run the business.

hook: One initiative vs. coordinated related initiatives
leftMeaning: A temporary initiative focused on a specific outcome or deliverable.
rightMeaning: A coordinated group of related projects managed together to obtain benefits not available from managing them separately.
trap: A program is not simply a very large project.
memory: PROJECT = outcome. PROGRAM = coordinated benefits.

leftMeaning: Coordinates related projects and activities to realize combined benefits.
rightMeaning: Groups projects, programs, and other work to support organizational strategy; components do not have to be directly related.
trap: Portfolio selection is driven by strategic alignment, not by operational similarity.
memory: PROGRAM = benefits. PORTFOLIO = strategy.

leftMeaning: A restriction or limitation that narrows available options, such as budget, deadline, regulation, or resource limits.
rightMeaning: A factor believed to be true for planning purposes even though it may not yet be proven.
trap: Both can change, but constraints restrict choices while assumptions shape plans under uncertainty.
memory: CONSTRAINT = limits us. ASSUMPTION = we believe it for planning.

leftMeaning: Raw project observations or measurements without interpretation.
rightMeaning: Data that has been processed, analyzed, or contextualized so it supports understanding and decisions.
trap: Collecting more data does not automatically create better decisions; it must be analyzed.
memory: DATA = raw. INFORMATION = analyzed.

hook: What was produced vs. why it matters
leftMeaning: A product, service, result, or component produced by the project.
rightMeaning: The meaningful business or stakeholder benefit created by outcomes, not simply the existence of the deliverable.
trap: A completed deliverable can still fail if adoption or intended benefits do not materialize.
memory: DELIVERABLE = output. VALUE = business impact.
